chose: A reader can send the landing's mochi a hug, as the owner asked ("is it possible to also have a virtual hug animation loop. where if user double clicks the character a heart icon increments count of 'virtual likes' and the character does some cheap ceremonious animation, with debounce ofcourse") and then chose the option with no script and no count ("go with a. the key is a cheap animation, that keeps with the immersion and is also still not distracting, just playful"). The mochi is a button named "Send Mochi a hug". With no script, CSS cannot tell a double click from a single one, so a press stands in for it: the hug is :active and transitions, its look snapping in while pressed and easing back once let go, so every tap replays it and a second tap during it just starts it over, which is the debounce (nothing stacks, nothing is counted, nothing is kept). Chosen over a checkbox stack, which replays only as many times as it has boxes. Where the page moves (a wide screen with motion allowed), the mochi squeezes down, its antennas curl in and its eyes narrow to a smile, then it springs back as a heart (lucide's Heart, in the theme's own red, --destructive) rises and fades, about 1.2 s; each move is its own CSS property (scale, translate, rotate), so it rides on the idle loops instead of interrupting them. Everywhere else (the phone, less motion) the same press shows the heart, still, fading: a button that answered nothing would not be honest. From a keyboard, Space gives the hug (Chrome holds :active on a button while Space is down); Enter, and a screen reader, get nothing to see or hear, since the hug is all for the eye and the page has no script to answer a click. A per-view count is possible later with no script (CSS counters over a stack of checkboxes, capped and gone on reload); the owner left it out.
options: a press, on :active with transitions, replaying every time
a checkbox stack, each tap checking the next box, capped
a small script for a true double click and a count kept in memory
gray: What triggers the hug, how it looks, and where it runs are on the screen; the owner chose no script and no count, and the rest no check or earlier call settles.
undo: Render the photo slot's mochi without the .hug button, and drop the .hug rules, --heart and landingMochi's heart.
